description: This case study is the Steam Long-Range Plan of Consolidated Edison of New York, a 60-page document that looks at the company's district steam system, which serves over 1,500 buildings in New York City, through 2050. It sets four objectives, clean energy, climate resilience, core service and customer engagement, and expects to invest about $1.5 billion over ten years. Three pathways to net-zero emissions are compared, from full electrification to a hybrid with gaseous fuels. The resilience section reports more than $116 million invested in storm hardening since Superstorm Sandy and a climate vulnerability study with Columbia University that identified heat waves, flooding and cold spells as risks, with measures such as FEMA +5 flood standards, main valve replacement and advanced metering. Access: free PDF on the company website; no licence is stated. Coverage is the Con Edison steam service area in Manhattan. Caveats: only the executive summary and opening sections were read, and figures are the company's planning statements, not audited results. It suits adaptation planning and district energy resilience studies, and no directly related records are catalogued yet.
